video_title: Al Harrington joins the BAHA, Best All-NBA teams, Peyton Watson is a Cav and more

quotes.speaker: Al Harrington
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Harrington on how Don Nelson helped the Pacers stop Dirk Nowitzki
quotes.excerpt: Don Nelson obviously he just came from there he was a year removed so he knew everybody's strengths

text_blocks.speaker: Al Harrington
text_blocks.text: In the playoffs, Don Nelson obviously he just came from there he was a year removed so he knew everybody's strengths and weaknesses. He pretty much told us how to stop Dirk Nowitzki. And if you go back and look at the numbers, we really locked Dirk up as a team. It wasn't one person, but as a team we locked Dirk up.

text_blocks.speaker: Al Harrington
text_blocks.text: I don't know why you even mentioned that.

quotes.speaker: Al Harrington
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Harrington on the Pacers' 16-5 run to make the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: We had to win 16 out of 21 games just to make the playoffs
quotes.quote: We had to win 16 out of 21 games just to make the playoffs. And obviously when you win, I think we won exactly 16, so going into the playoffs with that type of momentum, we were hot as hell.

quotes.speaker: Al Harrington
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Harrington on why high schoolers should be allowed to enter the NBA draft
quotes.excerpt: Especially now with all the NIL stuff, they definitely should allow them to come back and go pro
quotes.quote: The kids are now going pro at 15, they're going to OTE, they're going to all these different things. Some of them are now feeling the pressure, especially because they're getting paid. You know what I'm saying? So some of them are now going to school early and have to be there on two-year contracts and stuff like that. So when you think about it, there were maybe 41 of us total that went pro from high school to the pros, and all of us were successful. Especially now with all the NIL stuff, they definitely should allow them to come back and go pro out of high school.

quotes.speaker: Al Harrington
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Harrington on the Pacers' 1998 lockout training camp
quotes.excerpt: Reggie Miller because they had just lost to Michael Jordan and them in Game 7
quotes.quote: Reggie Miller because they had just lost to Michael Jordan and them in Game 7 in 1998. They felt like they had the best team coming back with Michael Jordan retiring. Reggie is like, this is our year, we're going to win the championship. So while there was a lockout, Reggie kind of required everybody to come back to Indianapolis and just train and be ready for when the season started. Everybody came but two players, Dale Davis and Jalen Rose. Everybody else stayed and got their work in.

quotes.speaker: Al Harrington
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Harrington on Reggie Miller's work ethic and superstition
quotes.excerpt: Reggie Miller is probably the hardest worker that I've ever seen and most superstitious player I've ever seen
quotes.quote: Reggie Miller is probably the hardest worker that I've ever seen and most superstitious player I've ever seen. When I say he did the same thing the same way every single day, like he got to the gym at the same time every single day. He sat down the same way. He blew his nose, he'd take three pieces of tissue, and put it on his thigh like one, two, three, turn it, fold it, blow his nose, throw it away, put his socks on the same way at the same time on the clock every single day.

quotes.speaker: Al Harrington
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Harrington on the 1994 Knicks playoff loss to the Rockets
quotes.excerpt: 1994 when we were up 3-2 against Houston. I was 14 years old, freshman in high school
quotes.quote: 1994 when we were up 3-2 against Houston. I was 14 years old, freshman in high school, like Knicks, we fine, we about to, and we lose that series. I ain't going to lie, I cried when we lost Game 7. So just to let you know, that's how I've grown up, how much I've messed with the Knicks or whatever, but it was at that level.

quotes.speaker: Al Harrington
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Harrington on Jalen Brunson as the greatest Knicks player
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Brunson is for sure now the greatest Knickerbocker to ever play in New York City
quotes.quote: In my opinion, Jalen Brunson is for sure now the greatest Knickerbocker to ever play in New York City. I think once he's done playing, he will be. So he just got to stop.

quotes.speaker: Al Harrington
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Harrington on the importance of Jalen Brunson's contract
quotes.excerpt: I think that Brunson is going to be such a key to Philly and his communication
quotes.quote: I think that Brunson is going to be such a key to Philly and his communication to especially Jalen Brunson. And I don't know, and I mean maybe maybe you know him and Maxey got a good relationship too, hopefully they do because then he could be another one that can help him. But it has to be like, bro, you're going to get better, we just need you to defend, we need you to get offensive rebound, we need you to do all the dirty shit. Like if you do the dirty things, we are going to win at a high level.

quotes.speaker: Al Harrington
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Harrington on the need for team sacrifice to win championships
quotes.excerpt: You're not going to win this championship by yourself. It is not possible. Them days are over
quotes.quote: You're not going to win this championship by yourself. It is not possible. Them days are over. Like you have no chance. You're lucky to make the play-in. Because the play-in teams are going to fuck around and make it to the Western Conference Finals. You got to do these things to surround these great generational players with some got because you're not going to win this championship by yourself.

quotes.speaker: Raymond Felton
quotes.summary_phrase: Raymond Felton on why the Pacers' roster moves hurt their chances
quotes.excerpt: losing Mathurin and losing Miles Turner to me hurt them.
quotes.quote: The way Indiana played when they won, losing Mathurin and losing Miles Turner to me hurt them. They said, 'Zubac.' Zubac don't play the same way Miles Turner play. Miles Turner is face-to-the-floor, he can shoot. I just don't think it's the same with Zubac.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson breaks down the trade of Peyton Watson and Max Strus
quotes.excerpt: Peyton Watson has been traded to the Cleveland Cavaliers from the Denver Nuggets.
quotes.quote: There was a big-time trade yesterday. Peyton Watson has been traded to the Cleveland Cavaliers from the Denver Nuggets. The Denver Nuggets got back some picks, I believe, and Max Strus is headed to LA.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson discusses James Harden's new three-year contract
quotes.excerpt: James Harden just signed a three-year, $97 million deal.
quotes.quote: James Harden just signed a three-year, $97 million deal.

quotes.speaker: Charlie Villanueva
quotes.summary_phrase: Charlie Villanueva critiques James Harden's defensive effort in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: Anytime he shot the basketball, the person that was defending him got a layup on the other end.
quotes.quote: My only problem with James in that series was that anytime he shot the basketball, the person that was defending him got a layup on the other end, because he's just standing there or he'll follow his shot.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson on why Peyton Watson was a necessary addition for the Cavaliers
quotes.excerpt: Peyton Watson is a player that they needed bad because they were going out there with James, Merrill, Strus.
quotes.quote: I think Peyton Watson is a player that they needed bad because they were going out there with James, Merrill, Strus. He is a defender. You can't go out there with no type of defenders on the perimeter.

quotes.speaker: Charlie Villanueva
quotes.summary_phrase: Charlie Villanueva on Kevin Durant's scoring ability as a rookie
quotes.excerpt: I remember playing against him when he was in his rookie year in Seattle, and that motherfucker put on a show.
quotes.quote: I remember playing against him when he was in his rookie year in Seattle, and I think I was in Denver, and that motherfucker put on a show as a rookie. And the show never stopped. It just continued for 16 years or whatever year he's in. To this day.

quotes.speaker: Charlie Villanueva
quotes.summary_phrase: Charlie Villanueva chooses Kevin Durant over Carmelo Anthony as a scorer
quotes.excerpt: I'm going to go KD, just because I'll give him the edge that he's a better three-point shooter than Melo.
quotes.quote: I'm going to go KD, just because I'll give him the edge that he's a better three-point shooter than Melo.

quotes.speaker: Raymond Felton
quotes.summary_phrase: Raymond Felton's experience playing against Kevin Durant
quotes.excerpt: I played against him when he was in Seattle, and he was unstoppable.
quotes.quote: I played against him when he was in Seattle, and he was unstoppable.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson on the importance of opportunity in an NBA career
quotes.excerpt: Your opportunity dictates your career.
quotes.quote: Your opportunity dictates your career. I feel like I could have been a better player in different roles, right? And we also all know guys that we played with that, if they got a chance to play, them niggas was cold.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson on the impact of being drafted to a specific team
quotes.excerpt: I went to Indiana to a veteran team where they didn't need me for a year, three.
quotes.quote: I went to Indiana to a veteran team where they didn't need me for a year, three. So I kind of had to sit and wait and then had to play a role just to even get on the court. You understand what I'm saying? And that role that I played, it kind of dictated my whole career. It put me in like six man, come off the bench, you know, score, you know, get some points off the bench and then go sit down type of thing.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson on why LeBron James is the greatest basketball player
quotes.excerpt: Greatest basketball career is LeBron James, and it ain't even close.
quotes.quote: Greatest basketball career is LeBron James, and it ain't even close. It's not even like, that you can say not even close and stand by it.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson on LeBron James's career longevity and impact
quotes.excerpt: He's one of my biggest disappointments. I'm going to be honest with you.
quotes.quote: He's one of my biggest disappointments. I'm going to be honest with you. I feel like I could have been a better player in different roles. And we also all know guys that we played with that, if they got a chance to play, them niggas was cold.

quotes.speaker: Al Harrington
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Harrington on his former rivalry with Paul Pierce
quotes.excerpt: Paul Pierce and I are now friends. We became friends because we shared a joint at my daughter's birthday party.
quotes.quote: So what happened with me and Paul is that Paul Pierce and I are now friends. We became friends because we shared a joint at my daughter's birthday party. That's how we became friends after the basketball. I had a smoking room in the crib, so we smoked in the room. Me and KG. So that's when we became cool. But in my career, I fucking hated this nigga. I thought he was the corniest nigga on the planet. Every time we played, I just played like that. I couldn't stand him. I couldn't stand Antoine either. Antoine with all that shaking shit when he hit shots. I was rolling. I was feeling that. The competitive in me, because I'm competing against them during this time, I didn't like it.

quotes.speaker: Al Harrington
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Harrington on his toughest defensive assignments
quotes.excerpt: My toughest guard ever was Grant Hill. Grant Hill was cold before cold. My second toughest cover is Paul, and then my third toughest cover is Z-Bo.
quotes.quote: He was my toughest guard ever was Grant Hill. Grant Hill was cold before cold. Just he got, you know, had the ankle shit. My second toughest cover is Paul, and then my third toughest cover is Z-Bo. Those was my three. I had to everybody that I played. Z-Bo slow as hell. All post work, just no athletic move, no nothing. Just his superpower was that he kept his body on you the whole game. He was always on you, like wearing you down the entire game. You look up, son got 30, 16 rebounds. Yeah, those was my top three toughest guards.

quotes.speaker: Al Harrington
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Harrington on Victor Wembanyama's development
quotes.excerpt: He'll never get to Kareem's skyhook because he's too tall. All he's got to add is the dirt shot.
quotes.quote: He'll never get to Kareem's skyhook because he's too tall. But all he's got to add, which I heard he's adding, is the dirt shot. The dirt, poke, mid-post, fadeaway, leg, wrist, fadeaway. If he can, if he can make that his go-to shot, you can forget about it, bro. Wembanyama got too much shit. That's the problem. He's got too much shit. Once he figures that out, then he's going to be like, okay.

quotes.speaker: Al Harrington
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Harrington on his past rivalry with Kobe Bryant
quotes.excerpt: I played with Allen Iverson in the Big Three. We were the only team to go undefeated.
quotes.quote: I played with Allen Iverson in the Big Three. We were the only team to go undefeated. We were shacking Kobe in that bitch. So I did. So I mean I was Shaq, he was Kobe. But the motherfucker can score though. Give him his flowers. They could not fuck with us in that shit. We was just like, I really played like Shaq because at that point I was maybe out the league four years and I didn't want to get hurt, so I was just posting up the whole time. And then he was just on the perimeter going crazy. And then the next year this nigga comes back as a character, wearing a crown on his head and mask before every game and we lost damn near every game that year.

quotes.speaker: Al Harrington
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Harrington on why Michael Jordan is superior to LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: Whenever your peers acknowledge that they were afraid, they feared you. Those peers were dogs. These niggas was killers.
quotes.quote: Whenever your peers acknowledge that they were afraid, they feared you. Yes. Like these niggas was like killers. Yes. Killers. And when you had killers acknowledging that this nigga was the ultimate killer, you got to respect that. And I love LeBron, but we don't feel that way of like, of course he was great, but I never feared him. I never like didn't want to play him. Like Mike had niggas not wanting to play him. Damian Lillard told a story of the top 75, and this is in the motherfucker retired. When MJ walked in the room, it's different. He said it just went silent. No, it stops. It was actually Allen Iverson. That's coming from AI. He's like, when he walked in that room, we all look like, that's Mike.
